items.prompt: Which of these is a light source?

options.why: The Moon does not make light. It reflects light from the Sun.
A mirror reflects light. It does not make its own.
A spoon reflects light. It does not give out light.

hints: A light source makes its own light.
Some shiny things only bounce light back.
Ask of each one: does it make light, or just bounce it?
items.explanation: The Sun makes its own light, so it is a light source. The Moon, a mirror and a spoon only reflect light.

items.prompt: Sort these. Which are light sources?
hints: A light source gives out its own light.
Shiny or bright things may only reflect light.
Start with the Moon. Where does its light come from?
items.explanation: The Sun, a candle flame, a torch that is on and a glowing firefly make light. The Moon, a mirror, a window and white paper do not.

items.prompt: How is a shadow made?

options.why: That is reflection, not a shadow.
Glass is transparent, so it makes almost no shadow.
Objects do not give out darkness. A shadow is where light is blocked.

options.text: An opaque object blocks the light.

hints: A shadow is a dark area.
What stops the light getting there?
items.explanation: Light travels in straight lines. When an opaque object blocks the light, a dark shadow forms behind it.

items.prompt: Match each word to its meaning.
hints: Think of clear glass, tracing paper and cardboard.
Words starting with trans- let some or all light through.
Start with opaque. Can you see through cardboard?
items.explanation: Transparent materials let almost all light through and translucent ones let some through. Opaque materials let no light through.

items.prompt: Dina moves a puppet closer to the torch. What happens to its shadow on the wall?

options.why: Closer to the light, the puppet blocks more light, so the shadow grows.
The puppet still blocks light, so there is still a shadow.
Shadows stay dark. Their size changes, not their colour.

hints: Try it with your hand and a torch.
Close to the torch, the puppet blocks more of the light.
More blocked light means a bigger or smaller shadow?
items.explanation: The closer the puppet is to the torch, the more light it blocks. So the shadow on the wall gets bigger.

items.prompt: When is your shadow shortest on a sunny day?

options.why: The Sun is low in the morning, so shadows are long.
The Sun is low again in the late afternoon, so shadows are long.
At night there is no sunlight to make a shadow.

hints: Shadow length depends on how high the Sun is.
A high Sun makes short shadows.
When is the Sun highest in the sky?
items.explanation: The Sun is highest around midday, so shadows are shortest then. In Indonesia, the midday Sun is almost overhead.

items.prompt: A stick's shadow was measured during the day. What pattern do the results show?

head: Time
Shadow length (cm)
figure.alt: Table of shadow length: 8 a.m. 120 cm, 10 a.m. 60 cm, 12 noon 15 cm, 2 p.m. 60 cm, 4 p.m. 120 cm.

options.text: The shadow got longer all day.
options.why: The shadow got shorter until noon.

options.text: The shadow was longest at noon.
options.why: At noon it was 15 cm, the shortest.

options.text: The shadow got shorter until noon, then longer again.
The shadow stayed the same length.
options.why: It changed from 120 cm to 15 cm and back.

hints: Read the lengths in time order.
Find the shortest shadow. When was it?
What happened before and after that time?
items.explanation: The shadow was long in the morning, shortest at noon and long again in the afternoon. This happens because the Sun's height in the sky changes.

items.prompt: In the morning, the Sun is in the east. Which way does a tree's shadow point?

options.why: Shadows form on the side away from the light.
Shadows fall on the ground, away from the Sun.
A shadow always points away from the light source.

hints: A shadow forms on the side away from the light.
The Sun is on the east side.
items.explanation: Shadows point away from the light source. With the Sun in the east, the tree's shadow points west.

items.prompt: Choose 2 things you need to make a shadow.

options.why: A mirror reflects light. You do not need one to make a shadow.
A transparent sheet lets light through, so it makes almost no shadow.
You need light to make a shadow.

hints: A shadow is made when light is blocked.
items.explanation: You need a light source and an opaque object to block the light. A surface behind the object shows the shadow.

items.prompt: The Moon does not make light. It ___ light from the Sun.
hints: Think about what a mirror does to light.
The light hits the Moon and comes back to us.
The science word starts with r.
items.explanation: The Moon reflects light from the Sun. That is why we can see it at night.

items.prompt: Early one morning, a 1 m stick has a shadow 2 m long. At the same time, a flagpole's shadow is 10 m long. How tall is the flagpole?
hints: Compare the stick's height with its shadow.
At that time, every shadow is twice as long as its object.
items.explanation: At that time each shadow is twice the height of its object. The flagpole's shadow is 10 m, so the flagpole is 5 m tall.

solution.say: The stick is 1 m tall and its shadow is 2 m long.
So every shadow is twice as long as its object.
The flagpole's shadow is 10 m. Half of 10 is 5.

items.prompt: Draw a torch, a ball and the ball's shadow on a wall. Show the light as straight lines.

criteria.label: Puts the shadow on the side of the ball away from the torch
Labels the torch, ball and shadow

hints: Light travels in straight lines from the torch.
The shadow is where the ball stops the light reaching the wall.
items.explanation: Straight lines of light go from the torch past the ball. The shadow falls on the wall behind the ball, where light cannot reach.

items.prompt: Which materials let light through? Fill in the boxes.
hints: Transparent means you can see clearly through it.
Opaque means no light goes through.
items.explanation: Glass is transparent and wood is opaque. Tracing paper is translucent.
items.caption: Light and materials
head: Material
Type

items.prompt: Light travels in what kind of line?

options.why: Light does not curve by itself.
It does not go in circles.

hints: It does not bend by itself.
items.explanation: Light travels in straight lines. That is why shadows have clear edges.

items.prompt: Which object is opaque?
items.explanation: Opaque objects do not let light through. A wooden board is opaque.

items.prompt: Tracing paper lets some light through but you cannot see clearly. What is it called?

options.why: You can see clearly through transparent things.

hints: It is between clear and blocked.
items.explanation: Translucent materials let some light through but not a clear picture.

items.prompt: What happens to light when it hits a mirror?
items.explanation: A mirror reflects light. The light bounces off it.

items.prompt: Why is your shadow long in the early morning?

options.text: The Sun is low in the sky.

options.why: Heat does not change the length.

hints: Where is the Sun in the morning?
items.explanation: When the Sun is low, the light comes in at a slant and makes a long shadow.

items.prompt: Which clothing helps drivers see you at night?
hints: Drivers see light that bounces back.
Dark clothes are hard to see.
items.explanation: Reflective strips bounce a car's light back to the driver.

items.prompt: How can you make a toy's shadow on a wall smaller?

options.text: Move the toy closer to the torch.
Move the toy closer to the wall.
Cover the toy with tracing paper.
options.why: That makes it faint, not smaller.

hints: Closer to the torch is bigger.
items.explanation: A toy near the wall makes a smaller shadow. A toy near the torch makes a bigger one.

items.prompt: A torch is shone at a mirror and a bright spot appears on the ceiling. Why?

options.text: The ceiling is a light source.

items.explanation: A mirror bounces light in a new direction. It lands on the ceiling.

items.prompt: Does it make a shadow? Sort the objects.
items.explanation: Opaque objects block light and make shadows. Clear glass, clear plastic and air let light through.

items.prompt: Choose all the light sources.
hints: The Moon shines because of the Sun.
items.explanation: The Sun, a candle flame and a lit torch make light. The Moon and a mirror only reflect it.

items.prompt: Choose all the things that reflect light well.
items.explanation: Mirrors, foil and road markers are shiny and reflect light well. Black cloth and dark wood do not.

items.prompt: Match each light word to its meaning.
items.explanation: Reflect means bounce off. Transparent lets light through. Opaque blocks light and a source gives out light.

items.prompt: Order the steps to measure a stick's shadow through the day.
items: put a stick upright in the ground
items.explanation: Put the stick in the ground and measure the shadow in the morning, at midday and in the afternoon.

items.prompt: Light travels in ___ lines. A shadow forms when an ___ object blocks the light.
hints: Light does not bend by itself.
Clear things do not block light.
items.explanation: Light travels in straight lines. An opaque object blocks the light and makes a shadow.

items.prompt: Copy the results. 9 am 30 cm, noon 10 cm, 3 pm 28 cm.
head: Time
Shadow (cm)
hints: Read the numbers in the question.
items.explanation: The shadow was 30 cm at 9 am, 10 cm at noon and 28 cm at 3 pm.

items.prompt: Eko holds a toy at different distances from a torch. At 20 cm the shadow on the wall is 16 cm tall. At 40 cm it is 8 cm tall. At 80 cm it is 4 cm tall.

parts.prompt: What happens to the shadow as the toy moves away from the torch?
How tall is the shadow at 40 cm?

items.explanation: The shadow shrinks as the toy moves away from the torch. At 40 cm it is 8 cm tall.

items.prompt: A shadow is 30 cm at 9 am and 10 cm at noon. How much shorter is it at noon?
items.explanation: 30 - 10 = 20 cm shorter.

items.prompt: Tap the light source.

figure.alt: The sun is low on the left. A child stands on grass and a long dark shadow stretches to the right.

items.explanation: The Sun is the light source that makes the shadow.

items.prompt: Tap the object that blocks the light.

figure.alt: The sun is low on the left. A child stands on grass and a long dark shadow stretches to the right.

items.explanation: The child blocks the Sun's light, so a shadow forms on the ground.

items.prompt: A material that lets some light through but not a clear picture is ___.
hints: It is between transparent and opaque.
items.explanation: Translucent materials, like tracing paper, let some light through.

items.prompt: A cat's eyes shine in torchlight, but a cat is not a light source. Why do they shine?

options.text: They reflect the light from the torch.

hints: Where does the light come from?
items.explanation: The back of a cat's eye reflects light. Cats are not light sources.

items.prompt: A torch shines through four materials. A shows bright light. B shows dim light. C shows no light. D shows no light. Which are opaque?
hints: A and B let some through.
items.explanation: Opaque materials block all the light, so C and D are opaque.

items.prompt: A toy is placed 10, 30 or 50 cm from a torch. The wall stays put. Which gives the smallest shadow?

options.text: the toy 50 cm from the torch
the toy 10 cm from the torch
the toy 30 cm from the torch

hints: Closer to the torch is bigger.
items.explanation: A toy further from the torch makes a smaller shadow on the wall.
